verifications.claim: Artemis II is NASA's first crewed mission of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'It was the first crewed flight of the NASA-led Artemis program'; R3: 'Artemis II will be the first crewed mission of the Artemis programme'; R4: 'The first crewed Artemis flight'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Artemis II as the first crewed Artemis mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than April 1, 2026 from Kennedy Space Center, FL.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC ... Launch site Kennedy, LC-39B'; R2: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R3: 'Launch: April 2026 ... Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm launch on or after April 1, 2026 from Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will conduct a ~10-day lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Mission duration 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R3: 'Duration: 10 days'; R4: 'MISSION DURATION 9 Days, 1 Hour, 32 Minutes'; R6: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: ~10 days matches the reported 9-10 day duration.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will fly four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Crew size 4 ... crewed lunar flyby mission'; R2: 'loop around it'; R4: 'Crewed Lunar Flyby'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on lunar flyby trajectory.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test the Orion spacecraft's life-support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crew evaluated life support and other critical spacecraft systems'; R2: 'check out the Orion capsule ... life support systems'; R3: 'life support systems'
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of testing life support systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first human trip to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R2: 'first piloted moonshot since ... Apollo program 53 years ago'; R9: '53 years after Apollo 17'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first since Apollo 17 (1972), over 50 years.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Members Reid Wiseman Victor Glover Christina Koch Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list matches across sources.

verifications.claim: The duration of Artemis II is approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R3: 'Duration: 10 days'; R9: 'approximately 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: Precisely ~10 days confirmed.

verifications.claim: The goal of Artemis II is to test critical Orion spacecraft systems, including life support and manual piloting.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'validate the Orion spacecraft's systems, crew operations ... manual control'; R2: 'manually took control ... test to ensure certain capabilities'; R3: 'test the capabilities of the Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit testing of life support and manual piloting mentioned.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is to prepare for future Artemis lunar landings beginning with Artemis III.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface ... ahead of sustained lunar exploration in future Artemis missions'; R4: 'paving the way for future lunar surface missions'
verifications.reasoning: Prepares for future landings including Artemis III.

verifications.claim: The path of Artemis II is a free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'free-return trajectory'; R3: 'free-return trajectory'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory will take the crew around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'looping around the far side'; R2: 'far side of the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as far-side flyby.

verifications.claim: The maximum distance of Artemis II beyond the far side of the Moon is 4,700 miles.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'closest approach of about 4,067 miles (6,545 km) from the far-side lunar surface'; R6: 'as close as 8,000 kilometers (5,000 miles)'
verifications.reasoning: References give closest approach as ~4,000-5,000 miles; 4,700 is approximate but not exact match.

verifications.claim: Artemis II features the first woman (Christina Koch) to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Christina Koch the first woman ... to travel beyond low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated.

verifications.claim: Artemis II features the first person of color (Victor Glover) to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Victor Glover (an African-American) became the first person of color ... to travel beyond low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match.

verifications.claim: Artemis II features the first Canadian (Jeremy Hansen) to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen ... to travel beyond low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first Canadian/non-US.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a flyby mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crewed lunar flyby mission'; R4: 'Crewed Lunar Flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Terminology matches exactly.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is not a landing mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The crew will not land on the moon'; R2: 'will not land on the moon'; R9: 'The Artemis II crew will not land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm no landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis II aims to set a record for the farthest distance from Earth traveled by humans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'set the record for human distance from Earth, 252,756 miles ... breaking Apollo 13's record'
verifications.reasoning: Did set the record.

verifications.claim: Artemis II aims to exceed the Apollo 13 path.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'surpassed Apollo 13's ... record'; R6: 'surpassing the record ... set by Apollo 13'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly exceeded Apollo 13 distance.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test the Orion spacecraft's heat shield at 25,000 mph upon re-entering Earth's atmosphere.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 're-entered Earth's atmosphere at a maximum velocity of about 24,664 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Tested heat shield on reentry at ~24,664 mph; 25,000 is approximate.

verifications.claim: Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I flight in 2022.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After the uncrewed Artemis I mission in November 2022'; R2: 'An SLS rocket successfully launched an uncrewed test flight ... Artemis I'
verifications.reasoning: Confirmed as following Artemis I in 2022.
